Jordan,

Quick answers:
- We generally expect the beneficiary to receive the invoiced amount (i.e., payer to absorb intermediary fees). If that is difficult, we can accept net receipts but need a pre-estimate of expected deductions.
- OUR is preferred for USD payments, but our bank sometimes pushes back. If OUR isn’t possible we use SHA with a small fee allowance.
- For this invoice we’d prefer to pay in EUR via our euro sweep. We can do that if Redwood provides an expected FX conversion band and a small reconciling reserve.
- VAT: Globex will apply reverse-charge. We will need your VAT invoice and your VAT registration number on file.

Please include your bank template and any recommended text we should put in the payment instruction to reduce onward deductions.

Thanks,
Paulo

Hi all / Paulo,

Below is the recommended approach and two wire templates (shortened stubs) to address Globex's preferences while limiting short payments.

Top-level recommendation
- USD payments: request OUR if Globex’s bank will accept it. OUR avoids intermediary deductions and is the cleanest. If the bank cannot send OUR, instruct SHA but have payer add an explicit note: "Payer to cover all intermediary/correspondent fees — beneficiary to receive FULL invoiced USD amount." Include an estimated fee allowance.
- EUR sweep: accept EUR payment but add an FX reserve line (we recommend 1.5% of invoice) to cover conversion variance and any unexpected intermediary deductions. Reconcile the reserve on settlement once we see net landed amount. Alternatively, ask Globex to convert at their treasury rate and pay USD if they can — that removes our FX exposure.
- Intermediary fee estimation: for transatlantic EUR->USD/GBP->USD corridors, assume $15–$40 per intermediary leg depending on bank. For budgeting, use $25 per leg. If payment route involves two correspondent hops, budget $50.
- VAT: we will issue a VAT invoice with our EU VAT ID and mark it "Reverse charge — VAT to be accounted for by the recipient under Article 194 MOSS/Local law" (confirm legal language with tax). Provide VAT number: GB999999999.

Wire instruction (USD - OUR preferred)
- Beneficiary name: Redwood Inference Ltd
- Beneficiary account: 12345678
- Beneficiary address: 1200 Market St, San Francisco, CA 94103, USA
- Beneficiary bank: First National Bank
- Beneficiary bank SWIFT: FNBNUS33XXX
- Instruction: OUR — payer to bear all charges. Please include invoice number and our system reference: GLOBEX-INV-3899.
- Suggested payer note: "OUR charges — payer confirms payment of all intermediary/correspondent fees so beneficiary receives invoice amount in USD. Estimate per-hop fees: USD 25."

Wire instruction (EUR sweep - collect / beneficiary to receive net)
- Beneficiary name: Redwood Inference Ltd
- Beneficiary account (USD): 12345678 (as above)
- Beneficiary bank correspondent (EUR collection): EuroBridge Bank SA
- EuroBridge bank SWIFT: EUBRDEFFXXX
- Instruction: SHA/Beneficiary-net — payer to add estimated intermediary fee amount so beneficiary receives invoiced USD value after conversion.
- Suggested payer note: "EUR payment via treasury sweep. Payer requests beneficiary receive equivalent of USD invoice amount after FX conversion. Please add intermediary fees. Estimated per-hop fees: EUR 20 (approx)."

Operational steps / fallbacks
- If Globex can send OUR USD, there is no reserve required. If they send EUR, include FX reserve 1.5% on the invoice as a temporary line item and reconcile within 7 business days of receipt of funds.
- If a short payment occurs, ask Globex to provide bank trace (MT103 or confirmation). We will contact our banking partner to recover deductions; recovery is not guaranteed and may take 7–21 business days.

Attachments (sent): Redwood_wire_template.pdf (full bank template), payment-netting-matrix.xlsx (fee estimate by corridor).

Next steps for Jordan / Globex
1) Paulo to confirm whether their bank will support OUR for USD.
2) If not, confirm EUR sweep amount and whether Globex will add the 1.5% FX reserve line on payment.
3) Globex to send remittance advice after payment including trace code.

Paulo — happy to review language with your bank if helpful (I can join a quick 15-minute call to resolve OUR vs SHA).

Best,
Marissa Cole
